notes: The article explicitly ties Figure 1 to the Ag nanocrystal film transferred at 15–20 mN/m.
The ~3 µL stock drop is reported for most experiments, not specifically proven for this micrograph.
Study-wide 20–300 nm wire-width control and 1–2 µm wire lengths are not assigned as exact Figure 1 specimen measurements.
The article later amplifies the Ag wire mask and uses it to pattern PMMA/silicon; those downstream device outputs are not new Ag nanocrystal synthesis records.

structure_assets.description: Source Figure 1 FESEM image of the transferred Ag nanocrystal wire; 100 nm scale bar; PDF p.3 / printed p.1426. Publisher permission unverified.
Authored schematic of Ag nanocrystal spreading, self-assembly and transfer; not an experimental micrograph or a scale drawing.

quality.review_scope: Independent scoped quick audit accepted the selected main-text Ag nanocrystal self-assembly and transfer route, PDF pp.2–3 and Figure 1. Original nanocrystal synthesis is a cited prior method, not reconstructed; downstream device processing and SI remain outside this scope.
missing_fields: Ag-core synthesis, purification and size-selection parameters reside in cited method 11 and were not inspected.
Trough water volume/grade, assembly dwell time, compression profile and transfer speed are unreported.
The approximately 3 µL drop applies to most experiments; the exact Figure 1 aliquot is unidentified.
The Figure 1 wire has no sample-specific width distribution or crystal phase/atomic coordinates.
Downstream dithiol amplification lacks bath concentration/immersion time; PMMA and silicon patterning are outside this assembly scope.
conflicts: Text extraction renders the drop unit as mL; visual PDF p.2 clearly reads µL. The visual page governs the reported value.
